summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of tracheostomy, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and pressure ulcers was admitted for Foley catheter replacement and suspected urinary tract infection. He presented with fever, back pain, and hypernatremia. A chest X-ray showed bibasilar atelectasis with improvement from prior imaging, and urine cultures grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, though with possible contamination. He was treated with IV antibiotics, which were later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin based on sensitivities. His sepsis resolved, sodium normalized, and he remained afebrile prior to discharge. He was discharged to extended care on oral antibiotics with plans for INR and lab follow-up, continuing management of chronic conditions including diabetes, atrial fibrillation, and pressure ulcer care.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Septicemia due to gram-negative organism, unspecified
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, other speech and language deficits
